newsitem.title: USA: Court phone rule decision regrettable--FCC's Hundt.
newsitem.headline: Court phone rule decision regrettable--FCC's Hundt.

text.p: Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt said he regretted a court decision on Friday setting aside parts of the FCC's new phone competition rules.
"The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals decision today is a very regrettable setback for the purpose and intent of the 1996 Telecommunications Act," Hundt said in a statement.
"In several respects, the decision is wholly inconsistent with the mandate and intent of Congress," he said, adding that FCC planned to take the case to the Supreme Court.

Earlier on Friday, a federal appeals court said the FCC had exceeded its authority by setting reference prices for local calls as part of its efforts to pry open the $100 billion local phone market controlled by the Baby Bell phone companies.

The FCC rules spell out how new competitors can hook up to local phone networks, as well as the price the new entrants should pay for using the networks. The rules -- adopted last August but suspended by the court in the fall -- are meant to implement the communications law passed last year.
